subject.title: fix(telegram): polling worker pins a CPU core when the Bot API answers empty getUpdates instantly

question: Should OpenClaw accept up to one second of additional idle-to-first-message latency for Bot API endpoints that return empty `getUpdates` calls immediately in exchange for preventing the CPU busy loop?
rationale: The latency is an intentional consequence of the proposed polling cadence and cannot be removed without choosing a different product behavior or introducing a more complex mechanism.

options.title: Accept the bounded polling trade-off
options.body: Land the one-second empty-poll floor as the fixed safety behavior for endpoints that do not honor Telegram long polling.

options.title: Choose a different cadence policy
options.body: Ask for a different fixed interval or a design that changes the delivery-latency versus CPU-protection trade-off without adding an unnecessary user configuration option.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded polling trade-off
recommendation.body: Land the one-second empty-poll floor as the fixed safety behavior for endpoints that do not honor Telegram long polling.
